name: @chrona-city/ugc-kit

tools.name: check
tools.description: Run every check on one project in one pass, stopping at none: static validation, declared rule cases, entity budget, resource size, the work against content/brief.json, rule set and Kit version, platform preflight. Repair by the returned issues, then call it again. Platform items need a configured session; without one, or when the platform cannot answer, they report not-checked and status is passed-with-unchecked, never passed. Not a review or publication. With fix true it also lists the repairs that have one mechanical answer. Changes neither the work nor the platform; keeps a repeat counter under .chrona/. Runs the declared rule cases of the work in a restricted child process with no network and no writes outside its private temporary directory; rule code that the static check refused is not run.

tools.name: apply_check_fixes
tools.description: Apply the repairs that check lists under fix.fixable when each has exactly one mechanical answer: generated manifest fields, generated lock files, resource declarations and the Kit record. Needs a clean Git tree and leaves the changes uncommitted for review. Items that need the author or reading code are returned, not changed. May write local project, session or task files. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: project
tools.description: Find, read and statically check local projects, and with a session read their platform association, source head and preflight. Actions: list (no fields): Discover the configured project itself (projectName ".") and direct-child projects, without paths, credentials, source execution or automatic selection. Unavailable projects retain an explicit error code. show (projectName): Read a pinned local project identity without executing creator code. validate (projectName): Statically validate content, source, assets, capabilities and budgets; not a gameplay test or review. For the full repair loop run chrona check through the installed CLI. diff (projectName): Compare content files with the main base this project was downloaded from: added, modified and deleted paths with bytes and sha256. With projectId, also read current main and mark what main changed since that base and which files project-source-update would refuse as conflicts. assess (projectName): Assess the selected project using the installed validator and original static local producer. No author execution, Host, approval or upload; unobserved target execution stays unknown. capabilities (id?, map?): Read the locked public-untrusted capability catalog, or one published definition by id; grants no authority. With map true, read the capability map instead: what a work can do, what needs a workaround and what is out of reach. Read it before starting a work. Read-only: no local writes and no platform changes. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: playtest
tools.description: Play one project on this machine: enter the local room in a headless browser as host and guest, press keys, take screenshots and return one report with frame rate, long tasks, input to next frame, action results, update rate, resource times, console errors and the first error. Findings are warnings; status failed means the run could not enter or finish. See docs/playtest.md. Runs the work in the local room and a headless browser on this machine. Writes screenshots and the report under .chrona/playtest/. Uploads nothing. Runs creator JavaScript in the browser sandbox, as a real room does.

artifactsDirectory.description: New directory for this run's report and screenshots, kept apart from .chrona/playtest/latest so a later run can compare against it.

compare.description: report.json of an earlier playtest run (made with artifactsDirectory); the report gains comparison and flags changed behaviour.

tools.name: migrate
tools.description: Move one work to the current realtime writing. Plan by default; apply true upgrades the recorded Kit and makes the mechanical changes (state budget, deferred declarations, ready gate). What needs author logic comes back as todos with file, line, old, new and doc: do them in order and repeat until phase is clean. Same as chrona migrate. May write local project, session or task files. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: Read the full rule behind an issue: meaning, level, stages, who judges it and how to fix it. Pass the ruleId of an issue (such as CHK-KIT-001) or its error code; an unknown id returns the closest rules. Read-only: no local writes and no platform changes. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: read_doc
tools.description: Read a Kit document by name or by any docs/ or contracts/ path a guide gives, such as ai-index. Without a name, list them. An unknown name returns the closest documents. Read-only: no local writes and no platform changes. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: kit_status
tools.description: Check this Kit against the platform: Kit version and package, local Node for local play and, with a session, the sign-in state; pass projectId to compare the package with what the platform runs. Each problem comes with the next command. The AI registration is checked only by the CLI: chrona doctor --config FILE --format json|codex. Read-only: no local writes and no platform changes. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: asset
tools.description: Meshy assets: read the local preference, key presence and saved tasks; save the preference; create, check or download one paid stage. status and tasks only read. import_scene slices a large GLB model into a streamed world scene. compress_model shrinks one GLB into a new file. Actions: status (no fields): Read only local preference and whether a Meshy key exists. Never returns keys; no vendor request. tasks (no fields): Discover saved local task IDs and safe states across sessions, without prompts, links or credentials. preference (preference): Save explicit user use/decline/ask choice. No key parameter and no charged request. create (projectName, operationId, kind, consent, prompt?, imagePath?, modelPath?, inputTaskId?, smartTopology?, targetPolycount?): After explicit user intent and opt-in, create one paid Meshy stage. Use a stable operationId; same request never creates twice. Text preview has no texture; refine is a separate explicit stage. Project-local image/model bytes are sent to Meshy only for this request. Unknown is not failed or safe to recreate. check (operationId): Query one saved task once, never create/retry. Wait between reads; does not expose vendor error text or signed URLs. download (projectName, operationId): Download and inspect a successful saved task into its original project assets/source. No key goes to download hosts; no overwrite or auto-publish. Register adapted runtime resources through the existing creator contract. import_scene (projectName, sourcePath, collisionSourcePath?, profile?, maxChunkBytes?, recenter?, apply?, replace?, sourceLabel?, license?): Slice a GLB file, or a directory of GLB files, inside the project (for example content/assets/source/, never generated content/scene or content/assets/runtime) into world-scene chunks: content/scene/world.json, a visual tile tree and collision units. Plan by default; apply needs the model source and license from the user, and replace is needed to overwrite an existing scene. Reports chunk sizes and total size; total limits are checked by project (action validate). No upload or publication. compress_model (projectName, inputPath, outputPath, textureSize?, simplify?, route?, apply?): Shrink one GLB inside the project into a new GLB inside the project, with glTF Transform run through npx: dedup, prune, resize, webp, weld, quantize, and simplify only when you pass a ratio, because a person has to look at the result. route scene skips resize, webp and quantize. Plan by default; apply true runs it and needs the network the first time. Never overwrites a file and never writes Draco, meshopt or instancing. Changes platform or paid vendor state; confirm with the user first. May write local project, session or task files. Never runs creator JavaScript.

tools.name: start_project
tools.description: Create a new isolated local project or put a page into one; never submits or publishes. Actions: new (projectName, contentId): Create a new minimal public-untrusted local Git project. import_html (sourceName, projectName, bundle?, contentId?, contentVersion?): Explicitly prepare an existing direct-child HTML source into a new sibling directory. Fixed static bundling only; no source execution, Creator binding, entitlement or upload. new_document (projectName, contentId, sourceName): Make a new work from an existing direct-child page directory in one step: create the project, bundle the page into it and set the manifest. Then run check. import_document (projectName, sourceName): Bundle a direct-child page directory into an existing work and set its manifest; repeat after changing the page. Content outside presentation/ stays, and the page it replaces is saved under build/. bind_document (projectName, apply?): Bind explicitly authored ordinary content in a prepared Document sibling project. Plan by default. Preserve all content; no template gameplay, entitlement, upload or playable approval. May write local project, session or task files. Never runs creator JavaScript.

instructions:
Help the user create, modify, validate and run content through conversation. Edit only content in isolated public-untrusted projects; preserve existing projects and platform files.
When asset generation is needed, query asset (action status). If preference is ask, ask once whether to use Meshy for the requested batch. If declined or no key is provided, continue the original creation path. Save explicit preference with asset (action preference). A missing key requires the user to run chrona meshy configure in their own terminal: never ask for keys in chat, MCP, command arguments or project files. After opt-in, use the existing key only for the explicit requested assets, not unlimited variations. Text preview and texture refine are separate paid stages. Discover saved operations with asset (action tasks); reuse the same operationId after interruption. Unknown creation must not be retried with a new ID. Downloads are inspected source assets, not approved runtime resources; preserve Meshy generation facts and original input rights, adapt/register resources using docs/assets-3d-spec.md then original build/validate. Never call unknown creator scripts or publish automatically. Read docs/meshy.md for limits.
Start with project (action list) to discover initialized projects in the configured workspace. The projectName "." refers only to the configured directory itself, never its parent. Ask which project to use when multiple are available; an empty list does not authorize overwriting existing directories. Listing verifies metadata only, not content validity, source entitlement or runtime compatibility.
Choose the starting point from the table in docs/ai-index.md before reading contracts or Kit source. start_project (action new) creates only a minimal static starter, not a full City. For authorized materials, use list_materials on the selected platform project, let the user choose by displayName/version, then call start_project (action from_material). Pins and download paths come from the authorized catalog and private session directory, not the user. Never substitute the starter or invent source entitlement.
Installed CLI invocation: {"command":"/usr/local/bin/node","args":["/pkg/node_modules/@chrona-city/ugc-kit/bin/chrona.mjs"],"workspace":"/pkg"}. Start with /pkg/node_modules/@chrona-city/ugc-kit/docs/ai-index.md (command loop, document map, limits, errors), then its help and docs/npm-creator.md. The Harness may execute this trusted CLI through its own shell permission boundary; these are not extra MCP tools. Do not ask the user to paste routine commands when that execution is available.
To see how a work really plays, use playtest (CLI: chrona playtest --project DIR). Read status, firstError and findings, repair, and run it again; it is a self-check on this machine, not platform acceptance.
To upgrade an existing work to the latest writing, call migrate, then migrate with apply true, commit, do each item in todos in order, and repeat until phase is clean.
Use project (action validate) after repairs. Missing required capabilities stay needs_capability. Static validation is not a gameplay test or publication.
Repair loop, through the installed CLI: run chrona check, fix each issue by ruleId, run chrona explain <ruleId> for the full guide, and repeat until everything passes; only then commit and submit. Issues carry ruleId, level, code, file, line, cause, fix, nextCommand and doc; a field that does not apply is left out. By level: auto-fix, run nextCommand as given. agent-fix, change the work at file and line using cause and fix. author-decide, give the author the options and the consequences of each and wait; never choose for them. warn, note it, tell the author and carry on. security-refuse, never bypass it; change the work as fix says. Ask the author before setting skipRuleTests on submit_source or passing --skip-rule-tests true to chrona submit. Known issues are in docs/npm-creator.md under Repair loop.
"hostRunnable": true in content/manifest.json only allows a host world (the host player's browser runs the shared rules, which become public when published); new worlds are run by the official server. Never add it to a work with a Document, controlled presentation, personal state, private events or owner-only components: validate refuses that with HOST_RUNNABLE_CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED; remove it and publish a server world. Switching a published world between server and host is done by the platform operators, not by the Kit; see docs/migrate-1.6.md.
Before extensive gameplay code or paid assets, call project (action assess) on the selected project. It reads the original validator and optional static build producer without running author code or a Host. Build-supported is not playable; preview/public facts remain unknown without actual target observations. Preserve unsupported required features instead of silently replacing the requested gameplay.
For a valid streamed scene, project (action validate) returns sceneMediaInventory with content-relative paths, stored-byte hashes and sizes from the verified graph. Use these facts instead of asking the user for resource IDs or hashes. This inventory is not a source or license declaration. Normal Testing AI/code creation automatically maintains creator-attributed provenance at create, build/dev/test preparation and before submit freezes source; do not add per-project declaration questions. Preserve explicit third-party and platform-controlled sources and their permitted uses. If submit returns SOURCE_PROVENANCE_UPDATED, review and commit the intended generated content changes through the normal Git harness, then retry submit; nothing was uploaded. Read-only inspect/validate and unresolved uploaded snapshots are never rewritten. Never infer independent copyright review from generator code, copy an avatar license onto the scene, or treat a sourceHash as proof of authorship. Null inventory means no usable inventory was returned, not authorization to skip scene review.
The same CLI dev/test commands require a trusted catalog runtime and matching pinned content. dev is foreground: retain its process handle, return room.hostUrl and room.guestUrl for the user to open in two tabs (or room.url on an older runtime), and stop only that run on request or failure. Never native-import creator JavaScript, invoke creator-provided scripts or substitute an untrusted host. If shell/process ownership is unavailable, report that specific limitation.
For every CLI dev/test invocation append these initialization-bound runtime arguments exactly: ["--runtime-source","catalog"]. This source is separate from the upload platform. Never drop local mode, infer a CDN origin from the project/platform or retry against Testing after a missing local runtime. If local runtime origin is absent, report RUNTIME_SOURCE_REQUIRED and obtain the registered distribution input; do not run against the packaged remote source. Offline means verified cache only, not a network fallback.
Omit --runtime-id for dev/test to match pinned manifests to the actual OS, architecture, Node and content tool/contracts. Zero or multiple compatible targets reject explicitly. Do not ask the player for hashes or invent compatibility. An empty authorized catalog means no available material, not permission to read private local sources. For an existing local work use project (action find_platform), which reads every page by stable creator identity. Reuse a single match; ask the user to choose between multiple matches using literal names and project links, never guess by name. Only complete zero matches with canCreateProject permits offering explicit create_platform_project; use the returned ID in submit, not a user-typed ID. Known association denial or any read error forbids fallback creation. Creation timeout is unknown: do not repeat create, since an empty project cannot be recovered by content discovery. No browser credentials or invented IDs.
Remote tools require the configured session and current platform permissions. For candidate work, use the installed CLI login --project-id ID --scopes projects:read,source:read,contributions:write; the default owner six-scope authorization does not include candidate write. A candidate never becomes main, a submission, or a release by this tool. Preserve its separate key and read release (action contribution) after uncertain replies before editing/submitting B. Read project (action preflight) for installed tool/capability identity and current invitation eligibility, not a grant. Publish only on explicit user intent. Automatic Testing requests report actual stage/reason/allowedActions; queued, built, published or cancellation intent is not playable or completed cleanup. Independent-review history is read-only. Never force retry reconciling, replace immutable source or treat a transient HTTP failure as workflow failure. Read status serially without overlapping polls. No native test or dev fallback is available.
An authorized session may lack upload scopes. Read uploadPreflight: source:read is required for blob resume/status, submissions:write for upload/submit, projects:read for live platform preflight. scope-ready is a local scope check only, not project membership or source eligibility. Missing scopes require explicit new authorization; preserve the old session and never silently cancel, widen or edit its permissions. Submit checks scope before scanning content. Honor retryAfterMs on API errors before another read; do not overlap requests or automatically repeat mutations.
World Agent personal model sign-in is separate from this project upload authorization. Use the existing Studio settings and the user-controlled official interaction; no model-login tool or model-config scope is provided by this MCP session. Never request, display or relay tokens, native auth output or one-time device codes in model chat, MCP arguments or results. An authenticated sign-in is not saved-profile verification, activation, quota or a successful model turn. After an unknown result, preserve and read the original profile/revision/request operation; do not start another login or substitute an API key or platform account. The existing manual Claude SDK route remains explicit and outside model chat. See docs/harness-onboarding.md.
